principles: Fail-closed: widening the dedup key must never let a genuinely stuck loop escape the brake.
Never forge provenance: the breaker may stop and report, never auto-satisfy a gate or rewrite finding attribution.
Back-compatible by default: a reason with no structured signal keeps its historical key.
The diagnostic must be machine-actionable so an unattended agent can self-correct without a human.
drivers: An unattended run cannot obtain the interactive TTY ack the freeze demands, so a false-positive freeze is unrecoverable.
The existing breaker is load-bearing (B-bbaf) and its smoke must keep passing.
The distinguishing blocker information lives far beyond the 200-char slice, so the key must be widened, not merely re-tuned.

options.name: structured-signal-key
pros: Keys on a bounded vocabulary (bracketed reason codes + gap ids) so a real loop still repeats the same set
Leaves unstructured reasons on the historical key, so existing behaviour and its smoke are untouched
Small, local change inside the existing module
cons: Depends on gate reasons carrying structured codes; a gate emitting only free text gains nothing

options.name: raise-or-remove-the-200-char-slice
cons: Volatile tail content would leak into the key, so nearly every failure would look distinct and the brake would stop tripping at all

options.name: escalate-review-convergence-to-blocking
cons: It keys on a finding-count trend, not refusal identity, so it cannot see this failure mode at all
Turning an advisory into a hard block is a much larger behavioural change

rationale: Only this option distinguishes different blockers while keeping a genuinely repeated blocker on one stable key, which is exactly the fail-closed property the brake exists for. Raising the slice would widen the key with volatile text and effectively disable the brake; escalating review-convergence cannot observe refusal identity at all. The spike confirmed the existing module is the right choke point.

preMortem.scenario: The key widens so much that a real livelock never trips the brake
preMortem.trigger: Volatile free text leaks into the key basis
preMortem.consequence: The B-f458 class of 14-hour burn returns with no hard brake
preMortem.mitigation: Only a bounded vocabulary (bracketed codes + gap ids) enters the key; a smoke case asserts appending free text does not change the key

preMortem.trigger: The digest changes for reasons that carry no structured signal
preMortem.consequence: convergence-breaker-smoke fails or the brake mis-fires on unrelated stories
preMortem.mitigation: Signal extraction returns empty for unstructured reasons so they keep the historical prefix-only key; the existing smoke is re-run as a regression check

preMortem.scenario: The fix is asserted but never actually proven
preMortem.trigger: A test that only compiles against the fixed tree (missing-symbol failure rather than a behavioural one)
preMortem.consequence: A green suite that never demonstrated the defect
preMortem.mitigation: The smoke imports only pre-existing exports so it compiles against the unfixed tree and fails on an assertion; RED was captured before the fix and re-verified by reverting it
